newsitem.title: COMOROS: Politicians arrested ahead of Comoro Islands poll.
newsitem.headline: Politicians arrested ahead of Comoro Islands poll.

text.p: A former prime minister of the Comoro Islands was arrested on Saturday and an apparent arson attack destroyed a main administrative building ahead of elections for the state's federal assembly.
Police sources said Mohamed Abdou Madi was arrested along with the leader of the opposition Democratic Front party, Mustapha Said Cheikh.
There was no official comment on the arrests that took place a day before the Comoro Islands -- where there have been about 17 coups and coup attempts since independence in 1975 -- go to the polls.
Earlier the prefecture administrative building in the capital Moroni, which contained electoral material for the Grande Comore constituencies, was burned down.
This followed the burning down on Thursday of the offices of the governor of Moheli island, one of the four islands that make up the Comoros.
No one has claimed responsibility for these and other apparent arson attacks in the past two days.
The Comoro Islands go to the polls on Sunday to elect a 43-member federal assembly. The polls are being boycotted by opposition parties.

Some 76 candidates from the ruling National Rally for Development (MRD) party, Islamic hardliners of the National Front for Justice and a number of independent candidates will vie for the federal assembly (lower house) seats.

The opposition alliance, the Forum for National Recovery, says it wants the polls converted into elections for a constituent assembly, electoral registers revised and a new independent electoral commission put in place.
Some 313,979 people in the Comoro Islands' population of 510,000 are eligible to vote and a National Electoral Commission member has dismissed rumours the elections would be postponed.

Mohamed Taki, who was elected president of the Indian Ocean Islamic Republic in March, has banned the sale of alcoholic drinks except to diplomats and foreigners in hotels and has criticised women for wearing mini-skirts.
The federal assembly was dissolved last April and just over a month ago a controversial constitutional referendum gave most executive powers to the president.
The Comoro Islands are an archipelago of volcanic islands in the Mozambique channel 300 km (190 miles) northwest of Madagascar and 300 km east of the African continent.
There are four main inhabited islands -- Grande Comore, Ajouan, Moheli and Mayotte.
During the most recent political turmoil, in September last year French forces intervened to quash a coup led by veteran French mercenary Bob Denard.
The Comoro Islands have been in the headlines in the past week following the botched hijack of an Ethiopian Airlines plane, which crashed off the islands killing 125 people.
